title: Singleton contribution to a range flat map
statement: Let $N,K$ be natural numbers, let $b$ be a Boolean list, and let $c$ assign a Boolean list to each natural number. If $K<N$ and, for every $i<N$, $c(i)=b$ when $i=K$ and $c(i)$ is empty otherwise, then concatenating the lists $c(i)$ for $i=0,\ldots,N-1$ gives $b$.
hypotheses_covered: For every $i<N$, $c(i)=b$ if $i=K$, and is empty otherwise
